title: Microsoft 365 admin center: dedicated License Requests page for Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, documented actions, roles and self-service purchase controls are supported, including by the updated November announcement. The older Requests-tab path reaches the right page but should extend to the approval control; this is a minor correction.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center has a dedicated page for Microsoft 365 Copilot licence requests submitted by users.
claims.quote: We are introducing a new dedicated License Requests page in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center to help admins more easily discover, review, and manage Microsoft 365 Copilot license requests submitted by users.

claims.claim: Selecting License Requests from the Microsoft 365 admin center navigation reaches the dedicated page.
claims.quote: Open the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and select 'License Requests' from the navigation menu.

claims.claim: Automation for reviewing and approving or denying requests on the dedicated page is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph license requests approve deny self-service requests API PowerShell; Graph license requests self-service beta. Read release notes, manage-license-requests, Set-MgUserLicense and cloud licensing overview excerpts; assignment APIs do not document request decisions.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered table; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Billing > Licenses > Requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center reaches the existing self-service request process.
claims.quote: select Billing > Licenses. On the Licenses page, select the Requests tab. Select the row that contains the request you want to review. Assign licenses to each user through the default Approve the selected license requests option.
claims.fix: For the all-users approval route, extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Billing > Licenses > Requests > request > Approve the selected license requests > Approve'. Add to its note: 'Select all user checkboxes before choosing Approve.' Keep the qualification that this process is not confirmed as the new page. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/licenses/manage-license-requests.

claims.claim: An API for the existing self-service request review and approval process is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph license requests approve deny self-service requests API PowerShell; Graph license requests self-service beta. Read manage-license-requests, MSCommerce reference, Set-MgUserLicense and cloud licensing overview excerpts; none documents acting on this queue.

claims.claim: Settings > Org settings > Services > Self-service trials and purchases > product > Do not allow blocks self-service purchases and trials.
claims.quote: go to the Settings > Org settings page. On the Services tab ... select Self-service trials and purchases. ... select the product name. ... select Allow, Allow for trials only, or Do not allow.

claims.claim: Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled" disables self-service purchases and trials for that product.
claims.quote:
Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled"
Disabled | Users can't make self-service purchases or acquire trials for the product.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly established how the dedicated page relates to the older Billing > Licenses > Requests tab.
claims.quote: Searched: License Requests Requests tab replace retained admin center. Read release notes, manage-license-requests and November announcements, including its link to the request article; none explicitly identifies the older tab as the dedicated page or explains the relationship.

claims.claim: The November announcement says limit notifications include an upgrade option in most organisations.
claims.quote: Upgrade options: In most organizations, the limit notification includes an option to upgrade.

claims.claim: Users can use that upgrade option to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence from an admin who can approve or deny it.
claims.quote: Users can select it to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot license from their admin, who can approve or deny requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The self-service purchase setting affects whether users might see a direct purchase option alongside the upgrade request.
claims.quote: If the organization allows users to buy licenses directly, users might also see an option to purchase a license.

claims.claim: When users attempt a blocked self-service purchase, they can submit a licence request to the administrator.
claims.quote: When a user tries to make a self-service purchase for a product that you blocked, they can submit a request for a license to you, the admin.
